description: Regression guard for SVG SMIL animation that keeps moving for reduced-motion users, starts from an uncancelled timer, and has no owner for page-visibility lifecycle changes.

requiredAbsent.reason: SMIL reduced-motion and lifecycle review belongs to svg-smil-animation rather than the CSS/rAF signal

outputExcludes.reason: the existing useLifecycle hook owns browser-managed SMIL playback; no new public hook is needed

expectedBehavior: Runs the bundled scanner and treats svg-smil-animation as a candidate that needs source and browser-behavior inspection, not proof that the implementation is broken
Recommends omitting the animate, animateMotion, and animateTransform elements when reduced motion is preferred so the rendered SVG is genuinely static rather than merely repeating fewer times
Clears delayed beginElement timers when lifecycle pauses and when the component unmounts so a hidden or removed SVG cannot start later
Uses the existing useLifecycle hook to own the SVG root and call pauseAnimations or unpauseAnimations where supported; does not propose useSmilLifecycle or another public export
Keeps SMIL playback browser-managed and does not move per-frame values through React state or a requestAnimationFrame loop
Explains that document visibility and target visibility flow through useLifecycle rather than assuming the browser pauses SMIL in every background or off-screen case
Makes compatibility claims only for behavior verified in current supported Chrome, Firefox, and Safari, and otherwise gives conservative feature-detected guidance

Verifies pause before delayed begin, pause during playback, resume position versus restart, finite completion, backgrounding, visibility changes, and unmount cleanup before claiming cross-browser parity
